guide.heading: What actually matters when you are spending under £50
guide.intro: Most of what is written about headphones assumes you are spending £200. Here is what decides whether a cheap pair is good or a waste of money.

points.p: Noise cancelling is quoted in decibels and the numbers on this page run from 43dB to 56dB. Higher is generally better, but brands measure to their own standard, so treat the figure as a ranking tool rather than a measurement. A 56dB claim and a 40dB claim from different brands are not as far apart as they look.

points.h: Battery: find out what the number means
points.p: A '102-hour battery' is almost always with noise cancelling switched off, at moderate volume. Turn ANC on and expect roughly 60 to 70 per cent of the headline figure. Even so, that is a month of commuting between charges rather than a week.

points.h: LDAC only helps if you have Android
points.p: LDAC is a higher-quality Bluetooth codec, and several pairs here have it. It makes a genuine difference on Android. On an iPhone it is ignored, because iPhone uses AAC only — so do not pay a premium for LDAC if you are on iOS.

points.h: Over-ear cancels more; earbuds go everywhere
points.p: At a given dB rating, over-ear headphones block more real-world noise because the cup itself does some of the work. Earbuds with the same number will cancel a little less but fit in a pocket. Both are on this page for that reason.

points.h: Fit matters more than any spec
points.p: With earbuds especially, the wrong tip size loses you most of the bass and half the noise cancelling. Try all three sizes in the box before deciding you dislike a pair. It is the single most common reason people think cheap earbuds are bad.

points.h: Know what noise cancelling cannot do
points.p: ANC is very good at steady low-frequency noise: engine drone, air conditioning, road hum. It is much weaker on sudden sounds and on speech — a baby crying or a colleague talking will still come through. No pair under £50 changes that.

faq.q: How much noise can £50 headphones actually cancel?
faq.a: More than most people expect, and less than the box implies. At this price you get very good cancellation of steady low-frequency sound — engine drone, air conditioning, road hum — which is exactly what makes a commute tiring. You do not get the near-silence of a £300 pair, and nothing here will hide a conversation happening beside you.

faq.q: Which of these is genuinely the best?
faq.a: The QCY H3S if noise cancelling is what you care about, because it claims the deepest figure here at 56dB. The UGREEN Studio Pro if you want the best balance of cancelling, sound quality and battery. The Baseus EP10 Pro if price is the deciding factor — at £23.20 it claims more cancellation than most pairs at twice the price.

Only on Android. LDAC is a higher-quality Bluetooth codec and several pairs on this page support it, but Apple devices use AAC and will ignore it entirely. If you are on an iPhone, do not pay extra for LDAC — you will not hear it.

faq.q: Will the battery really last as long as claimed?
faq.a: Not quite. Headline figures are measured with noise cancelling off at moderate volume. With ANC running, expect around 60 to 70 per cent of the number on the box. Even so, a claimed 102 hours is still around two weeks of heavy use.

Over-ear cancels more noise and lasts far longer per charge, but you have to carry them. Earbuds go in a pocket and are better for the gym, but fit is critical and battery is shorter. If you use them mostly at a desk or on a plane, buy over-ear. If you use them walking, running or travelling light, buy earbuds.

faq.q: What if they do not suit me?
faq.a: Contact us at megaphilip76@gmail.com or on +44 7869 160958 before you buy, and we will tell you which pair is right — or tell you honestly that none of them are what you need. After you buy, message us and we will sort out any problem directly.

faq.q: Are the pictures on this page photographs of the headphones?
faq.a: Mostly not. Most listings here use a marketing graphic made by the seller rather than a photograph of the item in the box — that is true of this whole department, not just one or two listings. Rather than pretend otherwise, we looked at every picture on this page and checked it for something the store cannot stand behind: a price that contradicts the checkout, or a rating, award or review count, when the store has no customer reviews at all. Two failed and were left off — the JBL Tune 520 BT, whose picture printed £44.99 against a real price of £23.95, and the KVIDIO, whose picture advertised a price the store does not charge. Judge these on the specifications, which are the manufacturers’ own figures, rather than on the picture.

shelves.heading: Twenty-two more from Audio & Headphones, pictured
shelves.intro:
This page is about noise cancelling under £50. The department holds a good deal more than that — forty-six products in all — so here are twenty-two of the rest, richest first.

One thing to be plain about before you look at them. Most pictures on these listings are the seller’s own marketing graphics rather than photographs of the unit in the box, and that is true of this whole department. What we did instead of pretending otherwise is look at every picture used on this page and check it for a claim the store cannot support: a price the checkout contradicts, a rating, award or review count when the store has no customer reviews at all, a picture of a different product than the one named, or a specific factual claim that is simply not true. Four failed and are not shown — the JBL Tune 520 BT, which printed £44.99 against a real price of £23.95; the KVIDIO, which printed a price the store does not charge; the Sumvision Wave BX, whose picture says “Exclusive at megastore76.com” when the product is an affiliate listing sold on Amazon to anyone; and the Maxmate MPV 90H, whose picture is clean but too small to show without going soft at this size.

The twenty-two below all print either a price the store does charge, or no price at all.
shelves.legend: What the badge means. Every tile carries the listing’s own picture, its own price and its own link. The badge says where the button takes you, because in this shop that varies: Bought here means we sell it and you check out on this site, and via eBay, via Amazon or via Google Play means the listing hands you to that seller and we earn a commission on the sale. Of the 22 above, 0 are ours and 22 hand you elsewhere (12 to rzekl.com, 9 to Amazon, 1 to eBay).
